title: Critic loop workflow
summary: Use a generator and evaluator loop to improve a response against explicit criteria. This intermediate-level guide shows how to run the loop, handle failures, and verify that revision produced measurable value.
prerequisites: A task that can be evaluated against explicit criteria
A way to retain candidate responses and evaluator feedback for comparison

sections.title: When to use the loop
paragraphs: Use a critic loop when you can state clear evaluation criteria and expect repeated feedback to produce measurable improvement. Do not use the loop merely to collect parallel opinions, because its purpose is to revise a candidate in response to evaluation.

This guide uses critic loop as its label for a workflow in which a generator produces a response, an evaluator assesses it against stated criteria, and the generator revises it using that feedback. It is written for an intermediate-level reader who can define task requirements and compare successive responses.

sections.title: Run the loop
paragraphs: Step 1. Write the evaluation criteria and a stopping rule before generating the first candidate. Each criterion should describe an observable property of an acceptable response. This step has failed if a reviewer cannot determine whether a candidate meets a criterion. When that happens, rewrite the criterion as a specific test and apply it to a sample candidate before continuing.

Step 2. Have the generator produce a candidate, then have the evaluator assess that candidate against every criterion and provide feedback tied to the unmet criteria. Use that feedback to produce a revised candidate. This step has failed if the feedback is vague, contradictory, or disconnected from the criteria. When that happens, request a criterion-by-criterion evaluation with a concrete requested change; if contradictions remain, stop and revise the criteria before generating again.

Step 3. Repeat evaluation and revision only while the recorded results show improvement against the criteria, and stop when the stopping rule is met. This step has failed if a revision regresses, repeats an earlier defect, or provides no measurable improvement. When that happens, retain the strongest earlier candidate, stop the current loop, and revise the criteria or feedback before starting another iteration.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a record containing the criteria, the initial candidate, each evaluator assessment, each revision, and the reason the loop stopped. A final response by itself is not enough to demonstrate that the loop improved the work.

Verify the result by applying the same criteria to the initial and final candidates and recording the outcome for each criterion. Confirm that the final candidate meets more of the criteria or satisfies them more completely without regressing on criteria already met. If the records do not demonstrate improvement, do not claim that the loop succeeded; retain the best supported candidate and revise the criteria or evaluation process before trying again.
